From Vulgar Latin *pauta and cognate of English paw, of probable Germanic origin. Compare Galician pouta.

parole.significato: rat (any rodent of the genus Rattus)
parole.testo: From Vulgar Latin rattus (“rat”), of Germanic origin. Cognate to Galician rato and Spanish ratón. Mostly displaced Old Galician-Portuguese mur. The computing term is a semantic loan from English mouse.

parole.significato: to touch, to finger, to feel (tactually)
parole.testo: From Old Galician-Portuguese [Term?], from Vulgar Latin *toccāre, *tuccāre, of Germanic or onomatopoeic origin.
